3.2.3 
Calculations Required in the Controller 
For critical regulatory report items, calculations must be programmed in the PAC.   
3.3 
Data and Programs Backup and Disaster Recovery 
The PAC and SCADA programs are backed up routinely by the City of Greater Sudbury SCADA Group, 
and saved on CDs.  One copy is to be stored on site so it can be quickly reloaded in case any program 
becomes corrupt.  A second copy is stored in a secure, off-site location for the purposes of Disaster 
Recovery.  Any time these programs are modified, two copies of backups of the latest programs are to be 
made and labelled with new version numbers. 
The Data Backup strategy primarily covers the data files that are created within the SCADA system, 
typically daily files and/or scheduled reports. 
All data that is to be backed up is stored on the C:\ drive of the main HMI workstation and is to be located 
under the C:\iFIX_Public directory. The directory structure will exist and all files in the directory are to be 
backed up nightly. 
The data files identified are to be backed up weekly and copied to SAN. All backup data is to be retained 
for one year. 
3.4 
Data Management Submittals 
The following submittals must be made to the City: 
1. List of SCADA tags for historical data collection 
2. List of reports and definition of data to be included 
3. Draft reports 
4. Final reports

Summary of Site Activities – Final Rev 0   
 
Dear Agnes Wittmann:  
On behalf of the Orphaned and Abandoned Mines (OAM) Program of Manitoba Environment and Climate 
Change, Kontzamanis Graumann Smith MacMillan Inc. (KGS Group) has prepared this Summary of Site Activities 
describing the components and activities for on-going environmental management of the former Ruttan Mine to 
support closing the existing Environment Act License No. 858 VO.   
This report provides the following: 
x Site Description and Operational History 
x Closure and Remediation Activities/Infrastructure 
x On-going Water Monitoring/Management  
x Proposed Future Changes in Water Monitoring/Management 
1.0 SITE DESCRIPTION 
The Ruttan Mine Site is a closed mine located within UTM NAD 83, Zone 14V, Northing 6259596, Easting 459508, 
approximately 23 kilometers east of the Town of Leaf Rapids, Manitoba. Access to the site is via all-weather road 
Provincial Road (PR) 493, which transitions into Mine Road and leads directly into the site.

The main waterbodies on site are Ruttan Lake, Open Pit, Mill Pond, and Brehaut Lake, which are described as 
follows (see Figure 1). x Ruttan Lake was a natural lake prior to mine construction but has since been contaminated with Acid Mine 
Drainage (AMD) from mine tailings. Ruttan Lake is a submerged tailings storage area which requires water 
cover over the tailings to minimize the production of AMD water. The lake presently receives runoff from 
the surrounding undisturbed areas (west and south) and from overland flow that has come into contact 
with potential acid generating rock sources that are located around the Ruttan Lake, including relatively 
insignificant amount of waste rock used to build haul road (an approximately 2.5 hectare area). Ruttan Lake 
discharges into the Open Pit.

x Ruttan Lake was a natural lake prior to mine construction but has since been contaminated with Acid Mine

cover over the tailings to minimize the production of AMD water. The lake presently receives runoff from 
the surrounding undisturbed areas (west and south) and from overland flow that has come into contact 
with potential acid generating rock sources that are located around the Ruttan Lake, including relatively 
insignificant amount of waste rock used to build haul road (an approximately 2.5 hectare area). Ruttan Lake 
discharges into the Open Pit.  
x The Open Pit is a constructed waterbody that resulted from flooding the open pit mine and receives AMD 
impacted water from Ruttan Lake and any uncapped areas. The pit serves as a storage reservoir for water 
to be treated by the Water Treatment Plant (WTP).  
x Mill Pond was a natural pond prior to mine construction and during operation was used to store clean 
water for milling purposes. Currently, the pond serves as a polishing pond for treated effluent from the 
WTP. Water discharged from the north end of Mill Pond flows north through a discharge ditch/creek, under 
Highway 493 through two (2) culverts and eventually reaches Brehaut Lake. 
x Brehaut Lake was a natural lake prior to mine construction and was used as a settling pond for effluent 
from the water treatment system used during mining operations. Brehaut Lake also contains some 
submerged tailings, therefore it remains within the development limits. The lake is the most downstream 
water body on-site and therefore the overflow weir located north of the lake is the designated compliance 
point for all water discharged from the site.  
2.0 SITE OPERATIONAL HISTORY 
The Ruttan Mine was a base metal copper/zinc deposit initially mined as an open pit and eventually converted to 
an underground operation (Government of Manitoba, 2020). The property was owned and operated by Sherritt 
Gordon Mines from 1973 until 1987, at which time Hudson Bay Mining and Smelting (HBM&S) took over 
ownership. The mine, along with the mill, operated for approximately 30 years until closure in 2002. The area 
impacted by mining activities covers approximately 12 km2. HBM&S completed all of their closure obligations 
from 2003 to 2005. The closure activities included the removal of most of the buildings, dismantling and 
removing of any infrastructure owned by HBM&S, the capping of shafts and ventilation raises, and the removal 
of the headframe. Any concrete foundations were knocked down to ground level and basements and trenches 
were backfilled. HBM&S also constructed diversion dams and channels to direct clean water away from the 
contaminated areas of the site (HBM&S, 2002). ...

3.0 REMEDIATION AND CLOSURE ACTIVITES 
Since obtaining responsibility for site remediation in 2005, the Province of Manitoba initiated site rehabilitation 
activities by completing a project to revegetate the area of the former Ruttan Mill Site (an approximate area of 
19.8 hectares). Between 2006 and 2009, the Province retained KGS Group to provide engineering services 
involving physical inspections of several key features of the site such as dams, tailings areas, and diversion 
channels. Water level surveys within the Open Pit and a full Lidar survey of the site was also completed. In 2009, 
KGS Group developed a conceptual design study for the on-site water treatment.  
As part of the HBM&S Original Closure Plan, on-site AMD was directed to the Open Pit using the large 
(34,000,000 m3) volume of the pit and underground workings as storage for all on-site AMD water, anticipated 
to be for many years into the future. However, KGS Group’s survey showed that the open pit would reach its 
maximum storage capacity by 2014, versus the HBM&S forecast of approximately 2040. 
In October 2010, KGS Group was retained again to provide engineering services in support of mine closure 
activities. Initial activities were carried out in 2011 and included the following. 
x Collection and analysis of water samples from various bodies of water at the site. 
x Collection and analysis of samples of tailings and waste rock at the site. 
x Completion of a geophysical survey and geotechnical investigations such as test holes and test pits at the 
TMA dikes. 
The information from the site investigations were used to develop a revised closure plan that aimed to reduce 
risk to the surrounding environment from metals contamination at the site and minimize future operation and 
maintenance costs for the Province of Manitoba. Major components of the revised closure plan included the 
following items.  
x Grading of the TMA to direct clean surface runoff towards the south.  
x Stabilizing and grading of the downstream slope of West Dam to a slope of 4 horizontal to 1 vertical.  
x Capping of the TMA including exterior slopes of containment dikes with a low permeability clay cover to 
allow off-site discharge of run-off.  
x Raising the water level of Ruttan Lake by constructing an outlet control structure (North Control Dam) and 
raising the existing Ruttan Dam to provide a water cover over the tailing washout area adjacent to Ru...

Since 2005, the Province of Manitoba has assumed all property interest at the Ruttan Mine Site and is 
responsible for performing all ongoing rehabilitation work in connection with the mine closure.  
3.0 REMEDIATION AND CLOSURE ACTIVITES 
Since obtaining responsibility for site remediation in 2005, the Province of Manitoba initiated site rehabilitation 
activities by completing a project to revegetate the area of the former Ruttan Mill Site (an approximate area of 
19.8 hectares). Between 2006 and 2009, the Province retained KGS Group to provide engineering services 
involving physical inspections of several key features of the site such as dams, tailings areas, and diversion 
channels. Water level surveys within the Open Pit and a full Lidar survey of the site was also completed. In 2009, 
KGS Group developed a conceptual design study for the on-site water treatment.  
As part of the HBM&S Original Closure Plan, on-site AMD was directed to the Open Pit using the large 
(34,000,000 m3) volume of the pit and underground workings as storage for all on-site AMD water, anticipated 
to be for many years into the future. However, KGS Group’s survey showed that the open pit would reach its 
maximum storage capacity by 2014, versus the HBM&S forecast of approximately 2040. 
In October 2010, KGS Group was retained again to provide engineering services in support of mine closure 
activities. Initial activities were carried out in 2011 and included the following. 
x Collection and analysis of water samples from various bodies of water at the site. 
x Collection and analysis of samples of tailings and waste rock at the site. 
x Completion of a geophysical survey and geotechnical investigations such as test holes and test pits at the 
TMA dikes. 
The information from the site investigations were used to develop a revised closure plan that aimed to reduce 
risk to the surrounding environment from metals contamination at the site and minimize future operation and 
maintenance costs for the Province of Manitoba. Major components of the revised closure plan included the 
following items.  
x Grading of the TMA to direct clean surface runoff towards the south.

approximately 2.5 to 2.9 million m3 per year.

Lake. The tailings are capped with clay and vegetated. Surface water runoff from TMA Cell 2 is directed to TMA 
Cell 3 through rockfill lined ditches and swales. Cell 3 is located south of TMA Cell 2 and contains fine grained 
tailings that are contained by perimeter rockfill berms on the north, east and south sides and the West Dam 
adjacent to Ruttan Lake. The tailings are capped with clay and vegetated. Surface water runoff from TMA Cell 3 is 
discharged to the south through a constructed rockfill lined outlet weir (KGS Group, 2024a). Cell 3 is a low-lying 
area that generally had a soft subgrade that required stabilization by placement of 600 mm thick rockfill on a 
geotextile/geogrid to facilitate construction of the clay cap. 
3.1.1.2 West Dam and Seepage Collection System  
The West Dam is located on the west side of TMA Cell 2 and Cell 3 and along the east shore of Ruttan Lake. The 
slope of the West Dam was graded to a slope of 4 horizontal to 1 vertical and capped with clay and vegetated. A 
seepage cut-off wall, to prevent AMD seepage into Ruttan Lake, consisting of one row of VSP was installed 
through the tailings down to bedrock along the toe of the West Dam slope. The dam also includes a toe berm 
used as a lower access road.  
A SCS drain was also constructed at the upstream side of the VSP wall and the lower access road to intercept and 
collect AMD seepage coming through the West Dam tailings. The SCS was completed in 2022 with the drain 
routed north to divert the AMD seepage water to the Open Pit.

3.1.1.1 TMA Cells 
There are three cells within the TMA. Cell 1 is the eastern cell and contains mainly coarse tailings that are 
contained by perimeter rockfill berms on the north, east and south sides. The tailings are capped with clay and 
vegetated. Surface water runoff from TMA Cell 1 is discharged off site to the south through a constructed outlet 
weir lined with rockfill. Cell 2 is located to the west of TMA Cell 1 and contains mainly coarse tailings that are 
contained by perimeter rockfill berms along the north and south sides and the West Dam adjacent to Ruttan 
Lake. The tailings are capped with clay and vegetated. Surface water runoff from TMA Cell 2 is directed to TMA 
Cell 3 through rockfill lined ditches and swales. Cell 3 is located south of TMA Cell 2 and contains fine grained 
tailings that are contained by perimeter rockfill berms on the north, east and south sides and the West Dam 
adjacent to Ruttan Lake. The tailings are capped with clay and vegetated. Surface water runoff from TMA Cell 3 is 
discharged to the south through a constructed rockfill lined outlet weir (KGS Group, 2024a). Cell 3 is a low-lying 
area that generally had a soft subgrade that required stabilization by placement of 600 mm thick rockfill on a 
geotextile/geogrid to facilitate construction of the clay cap.

seepage cut-off wall, to prevent AMD seepage into Ruttan Lake, consisting of one row of VSP was installed

used as a lower access road.

collect AMD seepage coming through the West Dam tailings. The SCS was completed in 2022 with the drain 
routed north to divert the AMD seepage water to the Open Pit.

Brehaut Lake for mining operations to ensure adequate water cover over lime sludge that resulted from

water discharged from the site must meet water quality standards. There was no work completed at the 
dam included in site remediation works.  
The objective of the water management strategy is to minimize the volume of AMD water requiring treatment. 
Since the main source of AMD water is Ruttan Lake, the overall goal is to improve the quality of the water in 
Ruttan Lake until it is acceptable to be discharged directly to Brehaut Lake without treatment. Studies have 
shown that when AMD water freezes, the ice is relatively clean, and the metals concentrate in the water below 
the ice. In the winter, from early February to late March, the valve in the NCD is opened to allow the 
concentrated water below the ice to enter the Open Pit, while the relatively clean ice is retained in Ruttan Lake. 
In this way, the time for Ruttan Lake to achieve acceptable water quality standards is reduced. However, it is 
important that the water level in Ruttan Lake be maintained at 287.5 m or higher to maintain a minimum of 1.5 
m water cover over the submerged tailings delta.

The treatment plant includes an electrical room, office, lunchroom, washroom with sewage pump and holding 
tank, water sample testing station, and plant area that processes lime and clean water into lime slurry to treat 
the contaminated water from the Open Pit. The equipment consists of a slaker, mixing tanks with agitators, and 
reactor tanks and a lime storage silo. Seven progressive cavity pumps are used to move the lime slurry 
throughout the plant. Pumping station PS-1 is located west of the WTP on the east side of the Open Pit and 
consists of four submersible pumps and a structure to store electrical equipment. Pumping station PS-2 is 
located on the west side of the clean water reservoir and consists of a structure to store the clean water pump 
and electrical equipment.

The treatment plant includes an electrical room, office, lunchroom, washroom with sewage pump and holding 
tank, water sample testing station, and plant area that processes lime and clean water into lime slurry to treat 
the contaminated water from the Open Pit. The equipment consists of a slaker, mixing tanks with agitators, and 
reactor tanks and a lime storage silo. Seven progressive cavity pumps are used to move the lime slurry 
throughout the plant. Pumping station PS-1 is located west of the WTP on the east side of the Open Pit and 
consists of four submersible pumps and a structure to store electrical equipment. Pumping station PS-2 is 
located on the west side of the clean water reservoir and consists of a structure to store the clean water pump 
and electrical equipment. 
Clean water is pumped from PS-2 to the water treatment plant and is used for process water during the lime 
slaking process, and for flushing of plant equipment. Quick lime from truck shipments is added to the slaker or to 
the lime storage silo. The slaker mixes the clean water and lime to create a lime slurry. The lime slurry is then 
pumped into the mixing tanks. An agitator within the mixing tanks keeps the solids in suspension while a pump 
transfers lime slurry into the reactor to treat the contaminated water. The contaminated water is pumped out of 
the Open Pit from PS-1 into the reactors. The reactors mix the contaminated water and lime slurry, until it 
reaches a pH of approximately 10 units. The treated water discharges by gravity out of the water treatment 
plant into an excavated channel, which leads to the settling ponds. 
The WTP was designed to treat 20,000 m3 of acidic water in a 24-hour period over an annual operating 
summer/fall season of 150 days, for a total treatment capacity of 3 million m3. Modifications to the plant since 
commissioning in 2014 have increased the daily treatment capacity to approximately 30,000 m3/day and 
resulted in several changes to the configuration of the equipment and piping. Appendix A contains a set of as-
built drawings that were updated in 2023 to show the existing water treatment system.  
There is also a portable WTP that was installed during late summer of 2017 due to the extreme volumes of AMD 
and limited storage capacity for the AMD upstream of the Open Pit. The portable WTP is located just south of 
SP1 and operates in the same manner as the main WTP with a capacity to treat 20,000 m3 of AMD per day.  
In addition, a BNR Reactor (BNR) treatment system was installed and has operated at the site since 2021. The 
Reactor is owned by a third party and is not included as infrastructure of the Ruttan mine. The BNR involves a 
cylindrical reactor where lime is mixed with the AMD before being discharged to the sludge removal system. 
Treatment capacity of the BNR is unknown.

experienced third party operators, including startup in the spring and winterizing in the fall.

system is not designed to operate during winter months, and the operating season typically runs from late May 
to mid-October (100 to 120 days per year). The operation and maintenance of the WTP is handled by 
experienced third party operators, including startup in the spring and winterizing in the fall. The General Plant 
Operation Manual (Appendix C) describes the operating procedures and the operation and maintenance 
requirements for the WTP. A detailed Operation and Maintenance Manual is maintained at the WTP. 
At present, all water treatment activities at the Ruttan Mine Site are sub-contracted to Mine Water Recovery 
(MWR). Water treatment activities include operation of both WTPs and the BNR Reactor with a target total 
treatment volume of 5.5 million m3 (per operational season), operation of the valve in the North Control Dam to 
regulate water flow from Ruttan Lake to the Open Pit, and weekly compliance sampling at Brehaut Lake.  
Sludge management is sub-contracted to North Fringe of Saskatchewan to remove sludge from SP1, SP2, Mill 
Pond, and the bypass channel and pump the sludge into the Open Pit, with a target sludge removal volume of 
400,000 m3 (per operational season).

3 . 3 . 1 S I T E C O N D I T I O N A S S E S S M E N T 
The overall environmental management of the Ruttan Mine Site also involves an annual site condition 
assessment which includes the scope of work listed below:  
x Site Condition Assessment 
x Conduct one site visit every year starting in 2023 to inspect the overall site conditions, engineered 
covers, drainage pathways, and dikes in accordance with the National Orphaned/Abandoned Mines 
Initiative (NOAMI) Site Characterization Field Form.  
x Prepare a summary report to include a site plan, photographic documentation of the site conditions, 
completed NOAMI checklist, and recommendations for remedial works. 
The purpose of the site assessment is to ensure that all remediation components are in working order and to 
identify any deficiencies at the site that require attention. If deficiencies or repairs are identified, 
recommendations will be integrated into the summary report with a Class C cost estimate.  
4.0 CHANGES IN WATER MONITORING/MANAGEMENT 
Adaptive management of the water at the Ruttan Mine Site involves annual sampling of the water quality in 
Ruttan Lake. The water in Ruttan Lake is sampled and analyzed for the parameters specified in the federal Metal 
and Diamond Mine Effluent Regulations (MDMER) which are periodically updated. When the water quality in 
Ruttan Lake is in compliance with the requirements of the MDMER (approximately 5 to 10 years after 
completion of the TMA Cap in 2022), the invert of the weir at the NCD will be raised to 288.2 m and the caps on 
the pipes in Ruttan Dam will be removed. 
Compliance is considered to be achieved when the concentrations of all relevant parameters in the MDMER 
comply with the standards specified in the MDMER for 2 consecutive years. Sampling and analysis of the water 
quality in Ruttan Lake will be conducted annually to ensure that the water remains suitable for discharge. 
Proposed future changes in the frequency of water treatment and water monitoring will be based on water 
quality improvements observed in the site water bodies from the on-going mitigation measures implemented on

1.0 
OVERALL PLANT DESCRIPTION 
 
The Ruttan Mine Water Treatment Plant (WTP) is a low density sludge (LDS) system using lime 
to treat acid mine drainage The system comprises of a treatment plant inside a metal clad building, 
two pumping stations (PS-1 and PS-2), a clean water reservoir and 2 settling ponds. The treatment 
plant is located east of the open pit and includes an electrical room, office, lunchroom, washroom 
with sewage pump and holding tank, water sample testing station, and plant area that has two 
water treatment lines. Each treatment line processes lime and clean water into lime slurry to treat 
the contaminated water from the open pit. The equipment for each line consists of a slaker, grit 
remover, mixing tank with agitator, and reactor tank. Seven progressive cavity pumps are used to 
move the lime slurry throughout the plant. Ventilation fans and emergency shower stations are 
installed throughout the treatment plant. A central domestic water system with storage tank and 
electric hot water tank supplies water to plumbing fixtures and the emergency shower storage tank. 
Pumping station PS-1 is located west of the WTP on the east side of the open pit and consists of 
four submersible pumps and a seacan to store electrical equipment. Pumping station PS-2 is 
located on the west side of the clean water reservoir and consists of a seacan to store two clean 
water pumps and electrical equipment.  
 
The WTP is sized to treat 20,000 m3 in a 24 hour period, which is the equivalent of approximately 
3,700 US gallons per minute (USGPM).  Clean water is pumped from PS-2 to the water treatment 
plant and is used for process water during the lime slaking process, and for flushing of plant 
equipment.  Quick lime from truck shipments is added to each slaker, which mixes the clean water 
and lime to create a lime slurry. The lime slurry is then pumped through the grit remover and into 
the mixing tank. An agitator within the mixing tanks keeps the solids in suspension while a pump 
transfers lime slurry into the reactor to treat the contaminated water. The contaminated water is 
pumped from PS-1 into the reactors. The reactors mix the contaminated water and lime slurry, 
until it reaches a pH of approximately 10 units.  The treated water discharges by gravity out of the 
water treatment plant into an excavated channel, which leads to settling ponds north of the WTP.  
The two settling ponds operate in series to allow the solids to settle out as sludge.  The settled 
water discharges to Mill Pond, which provides final polishing before the effluent is released to 
Brehaut Lake through an excavated ditch.

NORMAL OPERATION 
 
The following is a general description for the normal operation of the water treatment 
plant. The reactor tanks and mixing tanks are typically run in a continuous operation 
whereas the slakers and grit removers are run on a batch system depending on the lime 
truck delivery. Remote controls for the various pumps and motors are located on the 
perimeter walls of the plant area, with the exception of the slaker and reactor vessels 
which have their own local control panels. 
 
2.2.1 
Lime Slaking Operation 
 
The slaking process starts with clean water from two pumps in pumping station PS-2 
being pumped to the water treatment plant. Operators at the water treatment have remote 
access to turn the clean water pumps ON/OFF via remote controls. The clean water is used 
to fill the slakers and flush equipment as required. Operators will open or close isolation 
valves throughout the piping to process the lime slurry and treat the contaminated water. 
 
Slakers are typically pre-filled by the operators prior to each shipment of quick lime. Once 
the lime truck arrives, the quick lime is blown into each slaker through an exterior cam-
lock connection. During lime transfer, the slakers must be operated to ensure mixing of the 
quick lime with clean water and to avoid the creation of lime clumps. Operators shall 
utilize the isolation valves to direct the quick lime to the correct slaker. Once loaded, the 
slakers are isolated from the piping. Operators shall ensure that the slakers remain in 
operation to ensure that the quick lime and clean water continues slaking. Slaking 
continues until the pre-determined temperature to ensure the proper amount of reaction 
between the clean water and the lime is completed.

from the slurry. To transfer the lime slurry to the mixing tanks, operators shall do the 
following: 
• 
Turn ON the motor and open the water supply to the grit remover; 
• 
Open the slaker discharge valve; 
• 
Turn ON the two progressive cavity pumps on both sides of the grit remover. The 
flow rate of each pump must be adjusted via the dial controls to ensure that the 
grit remover does not overfill or that the second pump is not run dry. 
• 
The mixing tank agitator motor is turned ON to keep the lime slurry suspended.

Rev. A 
 
 
 
Page 4 of 6 
 
from the slurry. To transfer the lime slurry to the mixing tanks, operators shall do the 
following: 
• 
Turn ON the motor and open the water supply to the grit remover; 
• 
Open the slaker discharge valve; 
• 
Turn ON the two progressive cavity pumps on both sides of the grit remover. The 
flow rate of each pump must be adjusted via the dial controls to ensure that the 
grit remover does not overfill or that the second pump is not run dry. 
• 
The mixing tank agitator motor is turned ON to keep the lime slurry suspended. 
 
Once all the lime slurry is transferred out of the slaker, clean water is added to the slakers 
and flushed into the mixing tank. Flushing the line ensures that lime does not harden and 
plug up the piping. Periodic manual cleaning of the slakers, grit removers, mixing tanks, 
and reactors may be required. 
 
2.2.2 
Contaminated Water Treatment Operation 
 
The lime slurry within the mixing tanks is continuously pumped into the reactor tanks to 
treat the contaminated water. The contaminated water is pumped from pumping station 
PS-1 into each reactor through the four submersible pumps. These four submersible 
pumps are controlled via a pump control panel in the electrical room or locally at PS-1. 
The flow rate of lime slurry transferred into the reactor will be adjusted by the operator via 
the pump controls on the north wall to meet a discharge pH of 10 for the treated water. 
This lime slurry flow rate will depend on the concentration of the lime slurry and flow rate 
of contaminated water. Operators must monitor and control this process at all times while 
the process line is in operation. 
 
Once the lime slurry and contaminated water are added to the reactor tank, mixers located 
on top of the reactor must be turned ON. These mixers will continuously mix both fluids 
to treat the water. The treated water will then gravity discharge out the reactor tank into 
14” HDPE lines that flow into the settlings ponds and eventually to Mill Pond and Brehaut 
Lake.  
 
Operators will be monitoring the equipment, piping, flow rates, and controls throughout 
the process. In addition, the facility will have to be kept clean through continual 
maintenance. Operators will also complete water sampling and testing to ensure treated 
water guidelines are met. In addition, periodic inspections of the dikes surrounding the 
settling ponds and ditches will be required. 
 
2.3 
WINTERIZATION 
 
The following is a list of items to be completed prior to shut down of the water treatment 
plant before winter. 
 
Perform maintenance storage procedures for all equipment as per Operation and 
Maintenance manuals. 
 
Perform pump rotation of all progressive cavity pumps once per month. Rotate fan 
by ¼ turn.  
 
Flush and drain all piping and equipment within the water treatment plant and 
pumping stations.

maintenance. Operators will also complete water sampling and testing to ensure treated 
water guidelines are met. In addition, periodic inspections of the dikes surrounding the 
settling ponds and ditches will be required. 
 
2.3 
WINTERIZATION 
 
The following is a list of items to be completed prior to shut down of the water treatment 
plant before winter. 
 
Perform maintenance storage procedures for all equipment as per Operation and 
Maintenance manuals. 
 
Perform pump rotation of all progressive cavity pumps once per month. Rotate fan 
by ¼ turn.  
 
Flush and drain all piping and equipment within the water treatment plant and 
pumping stations.

 
Provide portable air compressors to blow out all piping to remove standing water 
within the piping system. 
 
Manually operate all valves to the closed position. 
 
Lock-out main isolation valves at pumping stations (PS-1 and PS-2). 
 
Disconnect intake piping at pumping station PS-2 and properly anchor the intake 
piping and floats to the shore line.  
 
Cover the Active Filter in PS-1 with an insulated tarp. Plug in two space heaters 
into the dedicated heater receptacles adjacent to the active filter, and place them 
under the tarp facing the active filter. Use a metal frame or sheet of plywood to 
hold the tarp away from the heaters. Fasten the tarp to the plywood wall behind 
the active filter using wood screws. 
 
Cover all exterior vent openings (ie: slakers, ventilation fans, mixing tanks, and 
PS-1) with wooden boards to prevent access into the building by wildlife. 
 
Drain and blow out all domestic water piping and emergency shower piping 
within the water treatment plant. 
 
Pump out the sewage holding tank. 
 
Drain out 14” contaminated water and treated water lines.  
 
Test the satellite call-out system to ensure that it functions for all call-out 
scenarios, including unauthorized entry at PS-1, PS-2, the water treatment plant, 
or the auto-dialer enclosure, or in the event of a power failure. 
 
Winterization and off-site storage of the backup diesel generator. This includes 
but is not limited to the following: 
• 
Perform all manufacturer’s procedures for winterization of the diesel 
motor. 
• 
Disconnect all cables from the diesel generator to the water treatment 
plant. The shore power and control cable can be disconnected at both 
ends, rolled up and stored in the water treatment plant. The main power 
conductors should be removed from the generator breaker, coiled up and 
stored underneath the generator termination enclosure; 
• 
The generator shall be lowered off of its frame jack stands onto its 
wheels, and all blocking from underneath the generator removed; and 
• 
Transport generator to a secure location. 
 
Remove the pH probes from the piping and equipment. 
 
Store any spare pH probes in a heated enclosure, such as the pH analyzer 
enclosure or chart recorder enclosure. 
 
Shut down ventilation fans. 
 
 
 
3.0 
MAINTENANCE 
 
The following is a list of maintenance activities to be completed throughout the water treatment 
plant. 
 
Flush out water treatment plant piping system after every batch of quick lime has been 
processed.  
 
Check grease levels on slakers after each batch of quick lime and add additional grease as 
required. 
 
Dispose of accumulated grit from grit discharge after each batch of quick lime.

doc_payloads.parent_text:
PROJECT  OF MRPL CPP3 UNIT. 
Tender No: 3200000501                   Page 5 of 248                      Bidder Seal & Signature  
 
 
PMC SERVICES FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF SECURITY INFRASTRUCTURE IN MRPL, MANGALURU 
Phase-2: Tender Preparation, Vendor Evaluation and Bid Process Management 
for site LSTK contractor tender: 
 
         This phase will commence after management approval of deliverables in Phase-1 and 
shall involve the following: 
 
1. 
Preparation of tender including Technical and Commercial specifications  
2. 
Preparation of detailed engineering document which shall form part of the 
Technical specifications. 
3. 
Drafting Bid Qualification Criteria (BQC) – Technical and Commercial 
4. 
Assistance to MRPL in floating tender (Tender will be floated by MRPL) 
5. 
Attending pre-bid meeting to clarify queries posed by bidders 
6. 
Evaluating bids and coordination with bidders to ensure zero deviations or 
deviations that are acceptable. 
7. 
Arranging for presentations by bidders and technical demonstrations at site, if 
required. 
8. 
Coordinating with external agencies as required in seeking permissions for the 
demonstrations.  
9. 
Submitting Technical Recommendation report with respect to technically qualifying 
the bids by developing an evaluation framework to assess the technological 
feasibility.  
10. Assisting MRPL in commercial discussions with technically acceptable vendors 
prior to opening of price bids. 
11. Price Bid Opening recommendation to MRPL. 
12. Assisting MRPL in placing order on the successful bidder. 
 
Phase-3: System Implementation and Deployment 
 
1. 
Arranging for Kick-Off-Meeting with the successful site construction vendor. 
2. 
Finalization of deliverables for the vendor for implementation of the project 
3. 
PMC is responsible for integrated project management, support, monitoring, 
control, measurement, coordination and reporting for the total project with due 
focus on contractual schedule and quality control. 
4. 
Supervision of all activities of the project including engineering, design, supply, 
construction, testing and commissioning. 
5. 
Monitoring project progress and identifying, mitigating and resolving bottlenecks. 
 
6. 
Technically evaluate and accord approvals to the site construction vendor for all 
activities of the project including engineering, design, supply, construction, testing 
and commissioning. 
7. 
Ensuring quality during project execution. 
8. 
Shall organize and conduct monthly / weekly / daily progress reviews as required 
at locations which shall be mutually decided.

COMPLIANCE TO BID REQUIREMENT 
 
Bidders are requested to submit zero deviation bid, strictly as per terms and 
conditions of the Bidding Document. Bidder is required to confirm the same in the 
proforma provided in the Bidding Document. Stipulation or any deviation may render 
the bid liable for rejection. 
MRPL/ Owner expect the Bidder to comply with the requirements of the Bidding 
Document without any deviation and submit substantially responsive bid. MRPL/ 
Owner reserves the right to proceed with the evaluation if adequate nos. of techno 
commercially responsive bids have been received without raising any CQ/TQ. 
Therefore, it is expected that bidders submits total compliance bid. 
The deviation, if unavoidable, should be furnished as per FORM-D attached. 
Exception/ Deviations submitted elsewhere in the offer shall not be considered.  
19.2 
The Owner reserves the right to consider/ evaluate only substantially responsive 
tenders. A substantially responsive tender is one, which, in the opinion of the Owner 
(which shall be final and binding on the Tenderer(s)), substantially conforms to all the 
terms, conditions, specifications and requirements of the Tender Document without 
material deviations or reservations in respect of any of the following: 
- Scope, Quality or Performance of the work; 
- The Owner’s rights or the Tenderer’s obligations under the contract as per the 
tender documentation; 
- Such deviations the correction of which would affect the competitive position of 
other tenderers, who have submitted substantially responsive bids; 
- Any tender unaccompanied by the Earnest Money in a form which is not 
acceptable as per the Tender Documents, or falling short of the requirement of the 
Tender Document, shall be liable for rejection.

E) Jokatte West End gate on PP Road. 
F) Railway siding gate

A. MAIN GATE 
There are about 2200 to 2500 workers and approximately 300 visitors entering Main gate per day.  
 Following are the facilities required at Main Gate  
1. Separate entry and exit road with following infrastructure: 
a. Separate lane for 2-wheeler and 4 wheelers. 
b. Vehicle checking bay on both entry and exit side of the road with facilities for overhead 
checking. 
c. A security cabin for the Security IC to monitor the activities of the gate. 
d. Heavy duty boom barriers. 
e. Automated under vehicle scanning system with license plate reader  
f. Automated Tyre killers on both entry & Exit sides of the road. 
g. Armed sentry post on top of the gate complex. 
h. Rain shelter for the entire gate complex.  
i. 
Good amount of illumination with high mast lamps. 
2. Security gate complex to house the following infrastructure: 
a. Additional Pedestrian path way with canopy for Worker’s movement. 
b. Turnstile gates for automated access control compatible with Biometric /RFID readers 
ESSL iclock 990 finger version 10.  There should be a display system with suitable 
monitor for displaying the details with photograph of the person seeking entry. Quantity 
-6 
c. Multi-zone Door Frame Metal Detectors (MZDFMD) for detecting any metal objects 
(Ferrous or non-ferrous) hidden under the clothes. Additional Quantity required 3.

staff handing material movement. 
e. Secured Cloak room with racks/ cellphone lockers with token system for safe keeping 
of visitor baggage and Cellphones. 
f. Space for Visitor Pass & Contract workers pass section with corridor for contract 
workers and cubicles for the pass issuing authorities. 
g. Visitor’s Lounge / VIP Lounge 
h. Large parking area for accommodating vehicles of visitors, contract workers ,

F. Railway Siding gate: 
Railway siding gate is located near Thokur where the Railway wagons enter for loading coke.  This 
area will have two gates.  One for entry of Railway wagons and the other for entry of workers, 
employees and maintenance staff.  The following infrastructure needs to be provided at this 
location. 
1. A 12 feet high 1.5 Kms length boundary wall of RCC framed structure around the Railway 
siding area with razor wire overhang. 
2. Two numbers of watch towers to have a look of the entire Railway siding area at appropriate 
locations with proper approach with a pedestrian pathway leading from the nearest road.  
3. Two gate complexes, one for the regular entry of contract workers and other staff with following 
facilities: 
a. Proper sentry post with proper rain protection  for the entire gate complex. 
b. Two numbers of turnstiles (for entry and exit separately along with biometric readers). 
c. Good illumination of the entire area, along with the boundary wall and a the gates  with high 
mast lamps. 
d. The gate complex on the main entrance may be provided with communication facilities like 
telephone & Base Radio Stations. 
e. Drinking water facility and washrooms. 
4. Parking area for vehicles. 
 
G. CISF Township 
      The CISF Township needs to be provided with following infrastructure: 
1. There are two gates to CISF Township.  Both the gates should be provided with a sentry post 
with basic facilities like lights, fans and protection from adverse weather. 
2. The CISF Township needs to be provided with CCTV connectivity for their gates, outer roads, 
and perimeter etc. 
3. A children park needs to be developed in the CISF Township with swings, slides, see-saw etc. 
4. Vehicle parking sheds to park 4 Tata Sumo type vehicles, one truck and a bus.  
5. Boundary wall (of minimum 10 feet high) approx. 1.5 Kms to replace the chain link fence 
around the CISF Township with good amount of illumination.

EXHIBIT-2 
 
PMC’S SCOPE OF SERVICES  
OVERALL SCOPE OF WORK 
The Project Management PMC (PMC) shall carry out project management, with detailed configuration of 
project requirements, specifications, basic and detailed engineering, preparation, evaluation and 
finalization of site contractor tender, procurement services, inspection and expediting, supervision of 
project execution including construction, erection, pre-commissioning, commissioning and performance 
testing of the project and submission of final documentation to MRPL. 
 
PMC shall themselves fully prepare and shall be totally responsible for design, configuration, 
specifications, engineering and same shall not be sublet to the site contractor.   
 
The PMC or its any affiliates / business entities / related companies / subsidiaries / agents or any other 
entities where the PMC or its directors / officials have explicit / implicit interest cannot participate in the 
site contractor tender. 
 
In general, PMC shall act on behalf of MRPL (MRPL), report to the MRPL and be responsible for carrying 
out the Project complete in all respects. 
 
 
1. 
PMC’s Scope of Work 
Part 1 
 
Currently following services are envisaged under pre-project services scope:  
1. Engineering  
2. Plot Plan Preparation 
3. Site Related Studies 
4. Project Activities 
 
1) Engineering  
i. Preparation of Engineering Design Basis and Document(s) for the project in consultation with 
MRPL.  PMC shall prepare detailed engineering documents and drawings which shall be the basis 
for the site LSTK contractor.  The LSTK contractor shall carry out any residual engineering if 
required for the project as desired by PMC during the course of the project. 
  
ii. PMC to use the Existing GCC of MRPL Projects. The SCC document shall be made for the 
individual Tenders in consultation with MRPL. PMC shall review the existing GCC and if any 
changes to be incorporated in the GCC for this project shall get approval for the same from the 
MRPL, and incorporate the same in the SCC. 
 
iii. Project Management Consultancy Services during tendering, order placement 
a. 
Preparation of engineering, specifications, data sheets and site contractor tender document 
(techno-commercial)  
b. 
Preparation of BEC/BQC for the site LSTK contractor tender 
c. 
Assisting in pre-bid meetings and replies to the queries raised 
d. 
Techno-commercial Evaluation of bids 
e. 
Preparation of technical recommendation

OVERALL SCOPE OF WORK 
The Project Management PMC (PMC) shall carry out project management, with detailed configuration of 
project requirements, specifications, basic and detailed engineering, preparation, evaluation and 
finalization of site contractor tender, procurement services, inspection and expediting, supervision of 
project execution including construction, erection, pre-commissioning, commissioning and performance 
testing of the project and submission of final documentation to MRPL. 
 
PMC shall themselves fully prepare and shall be totally responsible for design, configuration, 
specifications, engineering and same shall not be sublet to the site contractor.   
 
The PMC or its any affiliates / business entities / related companies / subsidiaries / agents or any other 
entities where the PMC or its directors / officials have explicit / implicit interest cannot participate in the 
site contractor tender. 
 
In general, PMC shall act on behalf of MRPL (MRPL), report to the MRPL and be responsible for carrying 
out the Project complete in all respects.

MRPL.  PMC shall prepare detailed engineering documents and drawings which shall be the basis 
for the site LSTK contractor.  The LSTK contractor shall carry out any residual engineering if 
required for the project as desired by PMC during the course of the project.

individual Tenders in consultation with MRPL. PMC shall review the existing GCC and if any 
changes to be incorporated in the GCC for this project shall get approval for the same from the 
MRPL, and incorporate the same in the SCC. 
 
iii. Project Management Consultancy Services during tendering, order placement 
a. 
Preparation of engineering, specifications, data sheets and site contractor tender document 
(techno-commercial)  
b. 
Preparation of BEC/BQC for the site LSTK contractor tender

Assisting in pre-bid meetings and replies to the queries raised

Techno-commercial Evaluation of bids 
e. 
Preparation of technical recommendation

responsible for the construction of plant facility.

construction work and provide necessary instruments to address identified schedule 
concerns. Monitor work progress and review progress reports prepared by site LSTK 
contractor, identify problems, foreseeable delay and corrective actions required. 
 
iii. 
Fix construction programs, time / billing schedules, targets etc with construction agencies and 
periodical review of the same. Identify the construction infrastructure and resource 
requirement 
 
iv. 
Review and monitor QA programme to ensure that construction work is in accordance with 
good engineering and construction standards and practices, drawings and specifications.  
Ensure that non-conforming work is rectified at the earliest. Field engineering as necessary, 
field supervision and inspection. PMC shall undertake surveillance of field inspection of site

CONTRACT WORKER’S SAFETY POLICY 
1. 
SCOPE : 
This policy is applicable to all the contractors and their employees working in MRPL. This is 
also applicable to sub-contractors, suppliers, vendors and visitors. All the contractors are 
required to ensure that they and their employees comply with relevant safety requirements 
as mentioned in this Safety Policy depending on the nature of work. This policy is not a 
substitute to the statutory rules and regulations and also the prevailing MRPL Safety 
Requirements. This is to further reinforce the existing Safety Standards in Refinery.

1. 
SCOPE : 
This policy is applicable to all the contractors and their employees working in MRPL. This is 
also applicable to sub-contractors, suppliers, vendors and visitors. All the contractors are 
required to ensure that they and their employees comply with relevant safety requirements 
as mentioned in this Safety Policy depending on the nature of work. This policy is not a 
substitute to the statutory rules and regulations and also the prevailing MRPL Safety 
Requirements. This is to further reinforce the existing Safety Standards in Refinery. 
 
2. 
REFERENCE :This document should be read in conjunction with following : 
- General Conditions of contract (GCC) 
- Special Conditions of Contract (SCC) 
- Job specifications 
 
3. 
SAFETY REQUIREMENTS FOR CONTRACTORS: 
 
- 
Contractor shall furnish Safety policy and Safety Manual of their Company and his track record in 
safety for past three years to the Engineer Incharge. 
  Contractor shall furnish details of their safety department with CVs of safety officers in his 
bid document to Engineer Incharge.  
 
-The contractor MUST employ Qualified Safety Officers as per the table below, having about 
5 years of relevant experience in chemical units or Petrochemical Plants or refineries, as 
per The Factories Act 1948 / Building and other construction workers (Regulation of 
Employment and conditions of service) Act 1996 and Central Rules 1998 / The Karnataka 
Factories Rules 1969. Contractor shall ensure that all his workmen are aware about the 
nature of risk involved in their work and have adequate training for carrying out their work 
safely. Such Safety Officers appointed shall be dedicated and responsible only for safety. 
They should not be given any other responsibility. The contractor and his sub-contractor, if 
any, shall comply with the instructions given by MRPL Engineer In- Charge or his 
authorized nominee regarding safety precautions, protective measures, house-keeping 
requirements etc. Engineer-In-Charge from MRPL shall have the right to stop the work of 
the contractor, if in his opinion, proceeding with the work will lead to an unsafe and 
dangerous condition. Engineer-In-Charge shall get the unsafe condition removed or provide 
protective equipment at the contractors cost, whichever is applicable.

safety requirements, norms, rules and regulations as per the Factories Act 1948 and Karnataka 
Factories Rules 1969, OISD Guidelines 207 and other OISD standards / guidelines and Indian 
Standards.

of MRPL immediately after the finalization of contract / placing of LOI / order. This will include 
Safety Policy, Safety Responsibilities at various levels, Formations of Safety Committees and 
meetings, Method statements, Job Safety Analysis (JSA), Safety inspections, various pre-
inspection checklists, Safety manuals, Safety Audits, Emergency Plans, Safety procedures to 
be implemented for all the activities, deputation of Safety Officers, enforcement of safety 
practices.  
 
 
- Contractor shall devise a procedure on Accident Reporting. All accidents including Near Misses 
and property damages to be reported as per the MRPL’s Accident Reporting Procedure in force. 
All Accidents including Near Misses to be communicated immediately to Engineer Incharge over 
  telephone / verbally / and later submit the accident report. All accidents must be investigated, 
classified, analysed & comply with the recommendations to avoid its recurrence. Monthly 
Accident statistics must be developed and circulated. Contractor shall maintain a register of all 
such accidents.

violation and heavy penalty shall be levied on the main contractor.

and Engineer In-charge from MRPL immediately.

tackles, welding generator that are to be used inside refinery are to be certified by competent 
authority. Statutory checks are to be carried out and records are to be maintained by contractors 
to ensure healthiness. These certificates will be regularly checked by MRPL engineer in-charge. 
 
 
- The Contractor shall ensure that all industrial consumables such as Oxygen, Acetylene, Argon, 
Nitrogen, welding electrodes etc. are approved by MRPL, tested and records maintained by the 
contractor as per Gas Cylinder Rules before they are used for the job. LPG for gas cutting 
purpose is not allowed. 
 
 
-The Fire prevention / protection and safety equipments (including Personal Protective 
Equipments) should be certified by MRPL engineer in-charge.

trench, whichever is more. Cutting shall be done from top to bottom. Under no circumstances 
under-cutting shall be done.

services and the works.

-   When workers are employed in sewers and inside manholes, which are in use, the contractor

The atmosphere inside the space shall be checked for the presence of any toxic gas or oxygen 
deficiency and recorded in the confined space entry permit, availability of standby person at  
 
    manhole must be ensured before the personnel are allowed to get into the man-holes. The 
manholes opened shall be cordoned off with suitable railing and provided with warning signals 
    or caution boards or barricade tape to prevent accidents. There shall be proper illumination in 
the night. 
 
 
11. PAINTING: 
-   Respirators shall be provided by the contractor for use when paint is applied, safety of personnel 
in vicinity also should be considered while painting. 
 
-  Overalls shall be supplied by the contractor to the workmen and adequate facilities shall be 
provided to enable the painters for decontamination at the cessation of work. 
 
-   All solvent-based paints, thinners shall be stored in separate well ventilated storage kept under 
proper surveillance. 
 
-  Smoking, open flames or sources of ignition / hot work shall not be allowed in places where 
paints and other flammable substances are stored, mixed or used. A caution board, with the 
instructions written in national / regional language, “SMOKING / HOT WORK – STRICTLY 
PROHIBITED” shall be displayed in the vicinity where painting is in progress or where paints are 
stored. Symbols shall also be used for caution boards. 
 
 
-  Suitable IS marked First Aid Fire Fighting equipments shall be kept available at a place where 
flammable paints are stored, handled or used. 
 
-  When painting work is done in a closed room or in a confined space, adequate ventilation shall 
be provided. Workers shall wear suitable supplied air type breathing apparatus. Work shall be 
carried out under a valid work permit. 
 
-   Epoxy resins and their formations used for painting shall not be allowed to come in contact with 
the skin. The workers shall use PVC gloves and / suitable barrier creams. 
 
-   Adequate ventilation shall be provided especially when working with hot resin mixes.

-   Prefabricated parts should be so designed and made that they can be safely transported and  
erected. 
 
-   As far as practicable the safety of prefabricated parts while erection should be ensured by 
appropriate means, such as provision and use of: 
 
a) Ladders; 
b) Gangways; 
c) Fixed platforms; 
d) Platforms, Buckets, boatswain’s chairs, etc. suspended from lifting appliances; 
e) Safety belts and lifelines; and 
f)  Safety nets or catch platforms. 
 
-   Ladders to be inspected fortnightly by experienced trained mechanical foreman and mechanical  
technicians and record of such inspection to be maintained. 
 
-   The boatswain’s chairs/ platforms used in structural erection to be inspected and checked once    
in fortnight and record maintained. 
 
-  In addition to the conditions of stability of the part when erected, when necessary to prevent 
danger the design should explicitly take into account: 
 
a) The conditions and methods of attachment in the operations of stripping, transport, storing 
and temporary support during erection; and 
 
b) Methods for the provision of safeguards such as railings and working platforms, and, when 
necessary, for mounting them easily or prefabricated parts. 
 
-   The hooks and other devices incorporated in prefabricated parts that are required for lifting and   
transporting them should be so shaped, dimensioned and positioned as: 
 
a) To withstand with a sufficient margin the stresses to which they are subjected; and 
b) Not set up in the part stresses that could cause failures, or stresses in the building not 
provided for in the plans. 
 
-    Prefabricated parts made of concrete should not be stripped before the concrete has set and 
hardened sufficiently to ensure the safety of the operation.

accidentally.

should be provided with safety devices such as railings and working platforms to prevent falls of 
persons.

shall be maintained by the contractor. Triplicate copy of such permits shall be submitted to 
MRPL.

equivalent material.

-   Under the working floor of the scaffolding the next lower floor should be left in position as a 
catch platform. 
 
-  Suspended outside platform (inspection scaffolds) should be provided as per the relevant 
standards as stated above. 
-   Use of Catch platforms, stairs, ladders and Iron rung, lifting tools, tackles and work with hot 
asphalt, tar should be carried out as per the procedures outlined in relevant ILO manual. 
  
-  Full Body Safety Harness (Safety Belt) with lifelines (of various sizes 2’, 5’ and 9’ double 
lanyards) and safety nets being used should confirm to relevant standards and are to be 
inspected, tested, periodically and records be maintained. Damaged safety belts and nets 
should be discarded, taken out of service and disposed off. 
 
-   Safety belts must be used while working at height. The life lines (lanyard) MUST be tied to firm 
support. Incase of absence of firm support provision of wire rope of adequate size tied with 
lifting tackles to be made to tie the safety belt life line (lanyard). 
 
-   All Safety belts to be inspected once in a month and damaged ones to be discarded. Suppliers / 
Manufacturers Discarding criteria of safety belts to be submitted to MRPL. The record of 
inspection and the results to be maintained. And a copy to be submitted to Engineer Incharge. 
 
 
-   The scaffolds to be inspected and certified by the competent mechanical Engineer before use 
and subsequently, at least once in a week. 
 
16. SAFETY OF ELECTRICAL WORKS: 
Before starting work in live electrical panels, proper electrical isolation shall be ensured. The 
same to be inspected by the electrical in charge and necessary isolation tag shall be attached. 
Proper electrical isolation permit system along with LOTO (Locking Out / Tagging Out) system 
shall be maintained by the contractor. Triplicate copy of such permits shall be submitted to 
MRPL. 
 
17. CATCH NETS: 
-   Where workers cannot be protected against falls from heights by other means they should be 
protected by catch nets. 
 
-  Catch nets should be made of good quality fiber cordage, wire or woven fabric or material of 
equivalent strength and durability. 
 
-  The perimeter of catch nets should be reinforced with cloth-covered wire rope, manila rope or 
equivalent material. 
 
-    Catch nets should be provided with adequate means of attachment to anchorage. 
-  Catch nets to be inspected fortnightly, tested and records maintained. Damaged safety nets 
should be discarded and record maintained.

21. WELDING AND GAS CUTTING: 
-   Welding and gas cutting operations shall be done only by qualified and authorised persons and

-    All the hoses used on compressed gas cylinders (Acetylene, Oxygen etc.) to be as per IS. 
-  Welding and gas cutting shall not be carried out in places where flammable or combustible 
materials are kept and where there is danger of explosion due to presence of flammable / 
gaseous mixtures. Contractor shall continuously monitor the area with Explosimeter / H2S 
meters. 
 
-  Welding and gas cutting equipments including hoses and cables shall be maintained in good   
condition. It should be checked daily by the user and fortnightly by the supervisor and recorded. 
 
-   Barriers shall be erected to protect other persons from harmful rays from the work. When 
welding or gas cutting is done in elevated positions / on trenches / inside refinery units, 
precautions shall be taken to prevent sparks or hot metals falling on persons or flammable 
materials (Welding booths shall be constructed). 
 
-  Use of proper PPEs by personnel involved in Gas cutting / Electric Arc welding should be 
ensured. Use of Welders Helmet with face shield by the welders is a MUST. 
 
-   Fire extinguisher shall be available near the location of welding operations. Valid permit shall be 
obtained before flame cutting / welding is taken up &comply with all the permit requirements. 
 
-   Contact of personnel with the electrode or other live parts of electric welding equipment shall be 
avoided. 
 
-   Extreme caution shall be exercised to prevent accidental contact of electrodes with ground.

-   All portable grinders shall be used only with their wheel guards in position to reduce the danger 
from flying fragments should the wheel break during the use.

order not to exceed the prescribed peripheral speed. 
 
-   Helmet with face shield shall be used during grinding operation. 
 
23. HOUSE KEEPING: 
 
The contractor shall at times keep his work spot, site office and surroundings clean and tidy 
from rubbish, scrap, surplus materials and unwanted tools and equipment. 
 
-   Welding and other electrical cables shall be routed as to allow safe traffic by all concerned. 
-  No materials on any of the sites of works shall be so stacked or placed as to cause danger or 
inconvenience to any person or the public. The Engineer-In-Charge may require the contractor 
to remove any materials which, are considered to be of danger or cause inconvenience to the 
public. 
 
-  At the completion of the work, the contractor shall have removed from the work premises all 
scaffoldings, surplus materials, rubbish and all sheds and sanitary arrangements used / 
installed for his workmen on the site. 
 
-  House keeping of the workplace shall be done strictly by the Contractor on daily basis or as 
required by the Engineer-in-charge. Contractor to collect all debris/ scrap and dump at 
designated Scrap Yard as defined by MRPL authorities. 
 
-   A separate house keeping team to be formed and made available round the clock.

-   Adequate number of duly calibrated Explosimters, Oxygen meters, Hydrogen Sulphide detectors 
(Portable / Fixed) or any other multiple gas detector should be made available at site by the 
contractor. 
 
-  Combustible materials like timber, bamboos, paints etc. shall not be used at MRPL site for 
scaffolding or for supports. 
 
Containers of paints, thinners and allied materials shall be stored in a separate room, which 
shall be well ventilated, and free from excessive heat, sparks, flame or direct rays of the sun.

PMC SERVICES FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF SECURITY INFRASTRUCTURE IN MRPL, MANGALURU
circuits, overheating etc. Installation shall not cause any hindrance to movement of men and 
materials. 
 
-  Materials for all electrical equipment shall be selected with regard to working voltage, load and 
working environment. Such equipment shall conform to the relevant Indian Standards. 
 
-  The minimum clearance to be maintained for all overhead lines along roads and across roads 
shall be as per the statutory requirements. 
 
-  Grounding conductor of wiring system shall be of copper or other corrosion-resistant material. An 
extra grounding connection shall be made in appliances / equipment where chances of electric 
shock is high. 
 
-  Electric fuses and / or circuit breakers installed in equipment circuits for short circuit protection 
shall be of proper rating. It is also recommended that high rupturing capacity (HRC) fuses are 
used in all circuits. The Earth Leakage Circuit Breaker (ELCB) of 30mA max capacity shall be 
provided in the circuits. (ELCB) of 30mA max shall be provided on each Extension board. 
 
-   Wherever cables or wires are laid on poles, a guard wire of adequate size shall be run along the 
cables / wire and earthed effectively. Metallic poles as a general rule, shall be avoided and if 
used shall be earthed individually. Anticlimbing guards and danger notices shall be provided on 
poles. Each equipment shall have individual isolating switches. 
 
-  Wires and cables shall be properly supported and an approved method of fixing shall be 
adopted. Loose hanging of wires and cables shall be avoided. Lighting and power circuits shall 
be kept distinct and separate. 
 
-  Reinforcement rods or any metallic part of structure shall not be used for supporting wires and 
cables, fixtures, equipment, earthing etc. 
 
-  All cables and wires shall be adequately protected mechanically against damages. In case the 
cable is required to be laid underground, it shall be adequately protected by covering the same 
withbricks, Plain Cement Concrete (PCC) tile or any other approved means and provided with 
cable markers. 
 
-  All armored cables shall be properly terminated by using, suitable cable glands. Multistranded 
conductor cables shall be connected by using cable lugs/sockets. Cable lugs shall preferably be  
 
    crimped. They shall be of proper size and shall correspond to the current rating and size of the 
cable. Twisted connections will not be allowed. 
 
-  All cable glands, armoring and sheathing of electric cables, metal circuits and their fittings, 
metallic fittings and other non-current carrying parts of electrical equipment and apparatus shall 
be effectively grounded. 
 
-  All the Distribution Boards, switches, fuse units, bus bar chambers, ducts, cubicles etc. shall 
have MS enclosures and shall be dust, vermin and water proof. ...

Tender No: 3200000501                       Page 155 of 248                   Bidder Seal & Signature 
 
PMC SERVICES FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF SECURITY INFRASTRUCTURE IN MRPL, MANGALURU
testing lamps and similar hand tools. Only wooden ladders shall be used to reach the heights in 
electrical work. 
 
-  No material or earthwork shall be allowed to be dumped below or in the vicinity of the bare 
overhead line conductors. 
 
-  Separate work permits shall be issued for individual group leaders working on the same system 
which shall be returned after the completion of the work to the Engineer-In-Charge. 
 
-  Before any maintenance work is commenced on electrical installations/equipment, the circuits 
shall be de-energised and ascertained to be dead by positive test with an approved voltage 
testing device. Switches shall be tagged or the fuse holders withdrawn before starting the work. 
Adequate precautions shall be taken in two important aspects viz. LOTO system to be followed. 
 
-   That there shall be no danger from any adjacent live parts and  
-  That there shall be no chances of re-energisation of the equipments on which the persons are 
working. (Tag out and lock out LOTO system to be strictly followed). 
 
-  While working on or near a circuit, whenever possible the use of one hand may be practiced 
even though the circuit is supposed to be dead. The other hand may preferably be kept in 
pocket. 
 
-   When it is necessary to touch electrical equipment (for example when checking for overload of 
motors) back of the hand may be used. Thus, if accidental shock were to cause muscular 
contractions, one would not “freeze” to the conductor. 
 
-  Operation of electrical equipment shall be avoided when standing on wet floor or when hands are 
wet. Rubber mats should be placed infront of Panels / Distribution Boards as per Indian 
Standrads. 
 
-  Before blown fuses are replaced, the circuit shall be locked out and an investigation shall be 
made for the cause of the short circuit or overload. 
 
-   When two persons are working within reach of each other, they shall never work on different 
phases of the supply. 
 
-  When structural repairs, modification or painting work are to be undertaken, appropriate 
measures shall be taken for the protection of persons whose work may bring them into the 
proximity of live equipment / circuit. 
 
-   It shall be ensured that the insulation and wire size of extension cords is adequate for the 
voltage and current to be carried. 
 
-  While tapping electricity from the socket, plug top must be used. It shall be ensured that no 
extension boards are over loaded while tapping. Only standard three pin plugs (Naked Wire is 
prohibited) shall be used for tapping electricity. Broken sockets/plugs shall be replaced 
immediately with good ones. Only joint free cables shall be used for connecting equipment/Use 
of apparatus. 
 
-   Floors shall be kept free from trailing electrical cables to avoid tripping hazard.

shall be de-energised and ascertained to be dead by positive test with an approved voltage 
testing device. Switches shall be tagged or the fuse holders withdrawn before starting the work. 
Adequate precautions shall be taken in two important aspects viz. LOTO system to be followed. 
 
-   That there shall be no danger from any adjacent live parts and  
-  That there shall be no chances of re-energisation of the equipments on which the persons are 
working. (Tag out and lock out LOTO system to be strictly followed). 
 
-  While working on or near a circuit, whenever possible the use of one hand may be practiced 
even though the circuit is supposed to be dead. The other hand may preferably be kept in 
pocket. 
 
-   When it is necessary to touch electrical equipment (for example when checking for overload of 
motors) back of the hand may be used. Thus, if accidental shock were to cause muscular 
contractions, one would not “freeze” to the conductor. 
 
-  Operation of electrical equipment shall be avoided when standing on wet floor or when hands are 
wet. Rubber mats should be placed infront of Panels / Distribution Boards as per Indian 
Standrads. 
 
-  Before blown fuses are replaced, the circuit shall be locked out and an investigation shall be 
made for the cause of the short circuit or overload. 
 
-   When two persons are working within reach of each other, they shall never work on different 
phases of the supply. 
 
-  When structural repairs, modification or painting work are to be undertaken, appropriate 
measures shall be taken for the protection of persons whose work may bring them into the 
proximity of live equipment / circuit. 
 
-   It shall be ensured that the insulation and wire size of extension cords is adequate for the 
voltage and current to be carried. 
 
-  While tapping electricity from the socket, plug top must be used. It shall be ensured that no 
extension boards are over loaded while tapping. Only standard three pin plugs (Naked Wire is 
prohibited) shall be used for tapping electricity. Broken sockets/plugs shall be replaced 
immediately with good ones. Only joint free cables shall be used for connecting equipment/Use 
of apparatus. 
 
-   Floors shall be kept free from trailing electrical cables to avoid tripping hazard.

33. LIST OF PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENTS:

Equipments. All Personal Protective Equipments used at site to be of approved make. 
 
34. MANDATORY FOR THE CONTRACTOR EMPLOYEES WHILE WORKING INSIDE 
REFINERY: 
* Deployment of adequate nos. of safety officers as per table above and making available the 
mandatory items as per the minimum list below is a MUST as a part of mobilization activity. 
 
1. Safety Helmet. 
 
2. Safety shoes (Conforming to IS standards with ankle protection, steel toe and anti-skid / 
acid, alkali and water proof soles). 
3. Hand gloves (Leather impregnated cotton hand gloves). 
4. Spectacle type goggles with toughened glass lenses, plain face shields with and without 
chin guards. 
The contractor must use the “ISI” marked Personal Protective Equipments specific to the job. 
It is mandatory to have minimum backup stock of all the PPEs in addition to what is already in 
use at site. 
 
35. SPECIFICATIONS FOR SAFETY HELMETS-HDPE: 
1. Helmet Safety Industrial HDPE white colour. 
2. Contractor’s Logo at front side. 
3. Conforming to IS 2925, ISI marked & DGMS approved. 
4. Nape strap type adj. type 6 point adj. head band & sweat band with 3/4"CottonChinstrap.  
* Green helmets for Safety Personnel and Red helmets for electricians to be provided and used 
by them. 
 
36. SPECIFICATION FOR FULL BODY SAFETY HARNESS) SAFETY BELT 
 
Full Body Safety Harness (Safety belts) must be double lanyard type with scaffolding hook 
having self closing latch (spring type).  
 
Different type of hooks to be available based on the nature of job / type of support. Safety belts 
should be ISI marked and should conform to IS 3521 and DGMS approved and stamped. 
 
Safety belts, safety straps, lifelines, permanent anchors and connections should both separately 
and when assembled: 
 
a) Be capable of supporting safely a suspended load of at least 450 kg (1,000 lb) ; and 
b) Have a breaking strength of at least 1,150 kg (2,500 lb). 
 
If hooks are used for attaching safety belts to fixed anchors, they should be self closing safety 
hooks of various types and sizes. 
 
When a lifeline or safety strap is liable to be served, cut, abraded or burned, it should consist of 
a wire rope or a wire-cored fiber rope. 
 
Safety straps should be so fastened to safety belts that they cannot pass through the belt 
fittings if either end comes loose from its anchorage.

Schedule of Work.  The project schedule shall be drawn in such a manner that it meets the 
requirement of the client. The project shall be monitored based on a control schedule, 
which will be 1 months ahead of contractual schedule. 
   
MRPL and PMC shall there after settle such work program and such settled program 
signed on behalf of the MRPL and PMC shall constitute “Time Schedule of Work” or 
“Schedule of Work” for the purpose of the Contract. To complete the job as per schedule 
PMC shall mobilize additional manpower based on the actual requirement at PMC cost. 
 
3. 
Approval of Program: 
MRPL shall, within 15 days of receipt of such program, notify PMC in writing that: 
i. The work program is approved with or without modification; or 
ii. The work program is rejected, in which case reasons for such rejection shall be 
given; or 
iii. Further information is required to clarify or substantiate the work program. 
 
Provided that if none of the above actions is taken within the said period of 30 days, MRPL 
shall be deemed to have approved the program submitted.  PMC shall, within 15 days of 
receiving notification under (iii), provide further information requested failing which the 
program shall be deemed to have been rejected.  PMC shall within 7 days there-after 
submit a revised program taking account of the reasons given for the rejection or 
incorporating the further information requested by MRPL.  After MRPL’s approval of such 
detailed program, PMC shall comply there with, provided that such program may there-
after be modified with MRPL’s prior, written consent.

62.0 
GENERAL GUIDELINES TO SUPPLIERS (AS APPLICABLE) FOR ENVIRONMENT AND 
ENERGY COMPATIBILITY 
 
MRPL is an organization which is certified to ISO 14001 Environment Management System 
and ISO 50001 Energy Management System and looks forward to its service providers to 
help them maintain the system that is designed for this purpose. 
All suppliers are to ensure compliance to the following while they are providing Materials to 
MRPL or providing services within the premises of MRPL . 
a) Ensure that the products supplied are Eco friendly (easily disposable as bio-degradable 
waste and the end of life or with a buy back condition), when not covered by PO 
specification. 
b) Products supplied should be non-polluting when in operation/service.  
c) Items supplied are to be energy efficient i.e. “Star rated”. 
d) Ensure that the packing and Packaging material used are disposal as bio-degradable waste 
or with buy back condition. 
e) Material Safety Data Sheets contain environment /energy related data /information on 
energy efficiency usage, storage, spillage and easy disposal. 
f) Specify action to be taken for spillages, if any to prevent contamination of air, land and 
water.  
g) Ensure that there is no threat to environment during transportation to and returns from 
MRPL, during delivery / while supplying materials. 
h) Material supplied should not lead to damage or harm to vegetation and greenery while 
usage and disposal. 
i) Supplier shall comply with all applicable regulations regarding the supplied Goods including 
all materials used and shall provide all information necessary by such regulation and/or 
requested by MRPL 
j) Supplier shall be responsible, where physically possible, to take the Goods back for the 
purpose of recycling them within the scope of the statutory requirements or to dispose them 
in an environmentally-friendly manner. 
k) Suppliers are to take action and comply with requirements when failures are intimated by 
MRPL and repeated failures /failure to act may lead to termination of contracts. 
l) Ensure that the noise and pollution levels of vehicles and equipment when used to deliver 
goods are as per regulatory norms and are subject to verification.

ENERGY COMPATIBILITY 
 
MRPL is an organization which is certified to ISO 14001 Environment Management System 
and ISO 50001 Energy Management System and looks forward to its service providers to 
help them maintain the system that is designed for this purpose. 
All suppliers are to ensure compliance to the following while they are providing Materials to 
MRPL or providing services within the premises of MRPL . 
a) Ensure that the products supplied are Eco friendly (easily disposable as bio-degradable 
waste and the end of life or with a buy back condition), when not covered by PO 
specification. 
b) Products supplied should be non-polluting when in operation/service.  
c) Items supplied are to be energy efficient i.e. “Star rated”. 
d) Ensure that the packing and Packaging material used are disposal as bio-degradable waste 
or with buy back condition. 
e) Material Safety Data Sheets contain environment /energy related data /information on 
energy efficiency usage, storage, spillage and easy disposal. 
f) Specify action to be taken for spillages, if any to prevent contamination of air, land and 
water.  
g) Ensure that there is no threat to environment during transportation to and returns from 
MRPL, during delivery / while supplying materials. 
h) Material supplied should not lead to damage or harm to vegetation and greenery while 
usage and disposal. 
i) Supplier shall comply with all applicable regulations regarding the supplied Goods including 
all materials used and shall provide all information necessary by such regulation and/or 
requested by MRPL 
j) Supplier shall be responsible, where physically possible, to take the Goods back for the 
purpose of recycling them within the scope of the statutory requirements or to dispose them 
in an environmentally-friendly manner. 
k) Suppliers are to take action and comply with requirements when failures are intimated by 
MRPL and repeated failures /failure to act may lead to termination of contracts. 
l) Ensure that the noise and pollution levels of vehicles and equipment when used to deliver 
goods are as per regulatory norms and are subject to verification.

offer and this LC meets the stipulated LC criteria).

entitled to claim benefit of purchase preference benefit as applicable for MSE bidders under 
PPP-2012.  However the exemptions from furnishing Bid security (EMD) shall continue to be 
available to such a bidder. 
iv. In view of the above 
a) The bidder’s quoted prices against various items of enquiry shall remain valid even in case 
of splitting of quantities of the items, except in case of items where the quantity cannot be 
split since these are to be awarded in a Lot or as a package or Group. 
b) While evaluating the bids, for price matching opportunities and distribution of quantities 
among bidders, the order of precedence shall be as under: 
• MSE bidder (PPP-2012) 
• PP-LC complied bidder (PP-LC) 
In case the bidder has not declared his status as to whether he is an MSE Bidder or PP-LC Bidder 
during bid submission, then he will be considered as non PP-LC compliant bidder and evaluated 
accordingly. No further correspondence will be made in this regard.

Preference under the Public Procurement Policy – 2012 (PPP-2012) for MSE bidders and 
Purchase Preference Linked with Local Content (PP-LC 2017) shall be exercised as under:

i.e., PP-LC 2017 for PPP-2012 and therefore, bidder will be required to furnish the option 
under which he desires to avail purchase preference. This option must be declared within the 
offer and in case bidder fails to do so although he is eligible for both the Policies, MRPL shall 
evaluate his offer considering PPP- 2012 as the default chosen option.

benefit under PP-LC 2017 (irrespective of the fact whether he furnishes the details of LC in his 
offer and this LC meets the stipulated LC criteria).

entitled to claim benefit of purchase preference benefit as applicable for MSE bidders under 
PPP-2012.  However the exemptions from furnishing Bid security (EMD) shall continue to be 
available to such a bidder.

• MSE bidder (PPP-2012)

1 
Preamble 
1.1 
In tune with Make in India (Mil) campaign in oil and gas sector, the Government has 
decided to incentivise the growth in local content in goods and services while implementing 
oil and gas projects in India, and 
1.2 
Whereas the Public procurement policy rests upon the core principles of competitiveness, 
adhering to sound procurement practices and execution of orders for supply of goods or 
services in accordance with a system which is fair, equitable, transparent, competitive and 
cost effective, and 
1.3 
Whereas, the local content can be increased through partnerships, cooperation with local 
companies, establishing production units in India or Joint Ventures(JV) with Indian 
suppliers, increasing the participation of local employees in services and training them etc. 
1.4 
Whereas incentivising enhanced local content in the procurement of goods and/or services 
in oil and gas business activities would lead to increased local industry content; 
1.5 
Therefore, the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG) has decided tostipulate the 
following policy for providing Purchase Preference to the manufacturers/ service providers 
having the capability of meeting/ exceeding the local content targets in oil and gas business 
activities; 
1.6 
This policy considers the Local Content (LC) as the added value brought to India through 
the activities of the oil and gas industry. This may be measured (by project, affiliate, and/or 
country aggregate) and undertaken through Workforce development and investments in 
supplier development through developing and procuring supplies and services locally. 
2 
Definitions 
2.1 
Oil and Gas Business Activity shall comprise of Upstream, Midstream and Downstream 
business activities. 
2.2 
Domestic products shall be goods and/or service (including design and engineering), 
produced by companies, investing and producing in India. 
2.3 
Local Content hereinafter abbreviated to LC means the amount of value added in India 
which shall, unless otherwise prescribed by the Nodal Ministry, be the total value of the 
item procured (excluding net domestic indirect taxes)minus the value of imported content in 
the item (including all customs duties) as a proportion of the total value, in percent. 
2.4 
Domestic Manufacturer shall be business entity or individual having business activity 
established under Indian law and producing products domestically. 
2.5 
Supplier of goods and/or provider of service shall be a business entity having capability of 
providing goods and/or service in accordance with the business line and...

L 1 price for remaining quantity and so on, and contract shall be awarded 
accordingly. In case some quantity is still left uncovered on Class I local suppliers, 
then such balance quantity may also be ordered on the L 1 bidder.
